title: The Company Lab Launches CO.LAB Q Commercialization Studio to Scale Quantum Startups - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Chattanooga accelerator The Company Lab launched CO.LAB Q, a 12-month quantum commercialization studio starting its first cohort in November 2026, with Quantinuum as founding compute partner, Davidson Technologies running a DoD track, Middle Tennessee Electric providing grid testing, and EPB Quantum supplying live optical quantum networking. The partner stack shows quantum startup formation organizing around three concrete demand channels — defense procurement, electric utilities, and QKD network field trials.

insights.claim: Chattanooga-based accelerator The Company Lab has launched CO.LAB Q, a 12-month quantum commercialization studio whose inaugural cohort begins in November 2026, covering quantum computing, networking, cybersecurity, sensing and control hardware with rolling applications.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dedicated quantum studio with a fixed November 2026 start is a datable marker for early-stage quantum deal flow in the US Southeast.
insights.locator: Chattanooga-based startup accelerator The Company Lab

insights.claim: Quantinuum is CO.LAB Q's Founding Compute Partner, giving cohort startups direct access to its trapped-ion quantum processors, the Nexus cloud platform, the Guppy programming language and technical simulation tools.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantinuum is seeding startups on its Nexus/Guppy stack at formation stage — a low-cost way to build ecosystem lock-in against IBM's Qiskit and rival toolchains.

insights.claim: Davidson Technologies is Founding Defense Track Sponsor for CO.LAB Q, mentoring startups on Department of Defense mission needs and providing access to its quantum laboratory, cybersecurity frameworks and pilot pathways through DIU and SBIR/STTR programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense non-dilutive funding and pilots remain the main early revenue line for quantum startups; a purpose-built DoD track signals where the studio expects cohort exits to come from.

insights.claim: Founding Utility Partner Middle Tennessee Electric will help CO.LAB Q startups validate quantum algorithms for power grid reliability, load forecasting and infrastructure resilience, giving quantum software teams a live utility use case rather than a synthetic benchmark.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Grid optimization is one of the few near-term quantum use cases with a real buyer; utility participation at accelerator stage is an early indicator of pilot budgets forming.

insights.claim: EPB Quantum provides the studio with optical quantum networking infrastructure via the EPB Quantum Network in Chattanooga, enabling startups to run field trials for quantum key distribution and quantum communications on a deployed commercial network.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Access to an operational metro quantum network is a rare asset — it makes Chattanooga a default location for QKD product validation in the US.

insights.claim: CO.LAB Q is backed by a regional support bloc including the Tennessee Valley Authority, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Vanderbilt University, the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga's quantum center facilities and the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: ORNL and TVA alongside a regional utility means federal lab, generation authority and distribution utility are all in one quantum cluster — an unusually complete energy-sector go-to-market path.
insights.locator: Supported by regional collaborators including the Tennessee Valley Authority
